record.original_question: Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is a partially ordered set, with elements called faces, that satisfies the standard axioms generalizing the face lattice of a convex polytope: it has a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) has the same length $n+2$, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags of $\mathcal{P}$, and $\mathcal{P}$ is called a $k$-orbit polytope when this action has exactly $k$ orbits.

When $\mathcal{P}$ is regular (1-orbit), fixing a base flag $\Phi$ produces distinguished generators $\rho_0,\dots,\rho_{n-1}$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, where $\rho_i$ maps $\Phi$ to its unique $i$-adjacent flag. In this case $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is a string C-group: it is generated by involutions satisfying string Coxeter-type relations together with the intersection condition
$$\langle \rho_i : i \in I\rangle \cap \langle \rho_i : i \in J\rangle = \langle \rho_i : i \in I\cap J\rangle$$
for all $I,J \subseteq \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Conversely, every string C-group arises this way, giving a bijection between regular abstract polytopes and string C-groups.

For a $k$-orbit polytope ($k \geq 2$) with a prescribed symmetry type graph, choose an analogous distinguished generating set for $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ obtained from a base flag together with selected flag-changing automorphisms or coset representatives encoding the orbit structure.

Problem. Formulate and prove an analogue of the intersection condition for such a distinguished generating set of the automorphism group of a $k$-orbit abstract polytope, characterizing exactly which groups, equipped with these generators and relations, arise as automorphism groups of $k$-orbit polytopes with the given symmetry type graph.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has seen significant progress: a 2023 paper (Hubard–Schulte, "All polytopes are coset geometries") characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes in terms of generators, relations, and intersection conditions tied to the symmetry type graph. Specific cases — two-orbit polytopes and 3-orbit polyhedra — have explicit intersection-property formulations. A general unified analogue for arbitrary k and arbitrary symmetry type graph continues to be developed, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: characterize automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes through generators, relations and intersection conditions tied to their symmetry type graph
status_evidence.claim: Provides a general characterization of k-orbit polytope automorphism groups via intersection conditions on a distinguished generating set, addressing the problem in substantial generality.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: For 3-orbit polyhedra, researchers find intersection properties that certain subgroups and cosets of the automorphism group should satisfy.
status_evidence.claim: The analogue of the intersection condition has been worked out explicitly for 3-orbit polyhedra.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Distinguished generators for automorphism groups of two-orbit polytopes are discovered, face stabilizer subgroups are determined.
status_evidence.claim: The two-orbit case has explicit distinguished generators and intersection-type conditions.
